_comment: GENESIS RULES (V2-633) — the engine's shipped BASE conversational rules. This file is the factory default every install starts from; the operator overrides any of it by just SAYING so (set_style_directive -> style_policy.apply_directive persists the override in <workspace>/config/style.json, applied on the very next turn). Nothing here is per-user data: user overrides never live in this file.

style._V2_713: Dos PREFERENCIAS que vivían como prosa en el bloque `ops` del prompt: cuántas frases habla y si ejecuta una acción por turno. `principles.md` las llama carril sobre el JUICIO — una receta de conducta —, y desde V2-633 hay dónde ponerlas: aquí, con el operador cambiándolas al decirlo. `max_sentences: 0` = sin límite; `one_action_per_turn: false` = puede encadenar.

consent._comment: CONSENT (V2-712) — THE ONE RULE that decides act-or-ask, layered exactly like `style`: these are the factory defaults, the operator overrides any of them by SAYING so, and the override lands in <workspace>/config/consent.json applied on the very next decision. The rule itself is in nucleo/consent.py and asks four questions in order: is a FACT missing, is there DOUBT about what will be touched, does the RADIUS exceed what he named, and only then is the CLASS sensitive enough. Nothing here is hardcoded in code: a widget declares `security` (all shipped widgets: standard) and an action may declare `sensitivity`.
consent._ask_at: The lowest level that asks for consent EVEN with a clear order, a resolved target and complete data. `critical` means only money leaving his accounts stops by class; everything else is decided by radius and by whether the engine has what it needs. Operator, 2026-09-16: «si le digo borra una cita de la agenda llamada tal, la borras y punto».
consent._unbounded_asks: A call that does not name WHAT it acts on, or that will touch more than one thing, asks regardless of level — V2-707's rail, born from 147 DELETE requests against his real calendar: «vacía la agenda» is not «borra la cita del dentista». This is a rail on the CONSEQUENCE and does not bend for convenience.
consent._classes: Standing rules per class: never | ask | allow. PRESET, never hardcoded — each one is the operator's to change by speaking, and `consent.set_class()` is what writes it. His own example is the first line: «por defecto no autorrespondemos ningún mensaje de ningún tipo. Eso es una regla de usuario que viene preseteada en el Génesis. Pero si el usuario decide cambiarla, que la cambie.»
consent._classes_calendar: V2-718 — the operator's own criterion, made into DATA instead of a rule in code: «esto que no nos hace ningún daño no necesita permiso; añadir a otra persona, cambiar de hora o hacer otras cosas sí que obviamente necesitan permiso». Sending the invitation for a meeting to the person it was agreed WITH, at an address they gave us themselves, adds nothing and takes nothing back: allow. Putting a THIRD person in the room, or moving an hour somebody else has already blocked, changes what was agreed with them: ask. WHICH of the two a call is belongs to the widget that holds the guest list (widgets/agenda/data.py::consent_scope), and the operator can flip either of these by saying so.

library._comment: The agent's OWN filesystem (V2-638). One root, a folder per kind of thing. These are the FACTORY defaults; the operator renames a folder or moves the root by saying so, and the override lands in <workspace>/config/library.json. Every widget reads paths from here instead of inventing its own — that is the whole point.
library.guide: Video and films go in video/, music and any audio in audio/, papers, books and PDFs in documents/, pictures in images/. downloads/ is the torrent client's own sandbox — it writes there and nowhere else; a finished file is filed into its folder by kind.

errands._comment: V2-683/V2-692 — ERRANDS with a third party. `shadow` TRUE = decide and LOG what it would say, send nothing. It shipped TRUE because autonomy that writes to real people in the operator's name is handed over after he has read a few of those rows, not on the strength of a green test suite. He has now read them and asked for the opposite, in his own words: the agent has to carry the errand end to end «sin que tú le digas más que el disparo de salida», and «no necesita confirmacion». So the default is FALSE. The flag stays: an errand still only ever writes to the ONE conversation it was born in, and flipping this back is one edit.

playbooks._comment: A BRIEFING per kind of errand, never a script: what «done» means, what has to be known before acting, how this kind of thing is done well, and what ends it without success. An errand whose kind is not here still runs (the generic path) — that is what keeps this a shortcut and not a fence. The operator overrides any of it in config/playbooks.json.

meeting.brief: Propón dos horas CONCRETAS dentro de la ventana que te dio tu operador, mirando lo que ya tiene ocupado. Acepta la primera que la otra persona confirme y no sigas negociando después. No propongas nada fuera de esa ventana salvo que el encargo nombre una alternativa. Cuando haya hora, dilo claro y una sola vez.

stop_when: piden datos que solo el operador puede dar
booking.brief: Pide lo que falta antes de comprometer nada, confirma con la otra parte el día, la hora y el número de personas, y no des por hecha una reserva que no te han confirmado.
